title: OpenAI retires gpt-5.4-cyber on 20 days' notice, where its policy sets months
source_used: FourWeekMBA (same story; MIXED Reality News blocked, HTTP 403 / Cloudflare)
key_facts: OpenAI's deprecations page has an entry for gpt-5.4-cyber dated 11 Sep 2026 with a shutdown date of 1 Oct 2026, according to FourWeekMBA, which read the page directly on 2 Oct 2026.
The 20-day interval is FourWeekMBA's own arithmetic; the page does not state 20 days or any notification date.
The entry says the model is deprecated and will be removed from the API on 1 Oct 2026 and tells users to migrate to 'the most capable cyber model available to you'; it names no replacement.

OpenAI's policy on the same page: unless safety or compliance concerns require a faster timeline, minimum notice is at least 6 months for generally available models and at least 3 months for specialised variants.
The page gives no reason for the short notice, does not say which tier the model is in, and does not say whether the safety or compliance exception was used.
Other 2026 entries on the page gave about 182 to 184 days of notice (97 days for text-to-speech models).
FourWeekMBA did not test the API and did not confirm that the model was actually removed.
quote_evidence: OpenAI’s own deprecations page shows an entry for gpt-5.4-cyber dated September 11, 2026, with a shutdown date of October 1, 2026.
The 20-day interval is computed by this publication.
The page gives no reason for the length of notice and does not say which notice category gpt-5.4-cyber falls in.
why_it_matters_hint: A published notice-period promise of months was followed by a roughly 20-day window, and the page gives no reason.
event_date: Deprecation entry dated 11 Sep 2026; shutdown date 1 Oct 2026.
notes: Original MIXED Reality News (2 Oct 2026, 16:25 GMT) was blocked (HTTP 403, Cloudflare page). Written from FourWeekMBA (2 Oct 2026), a business-analysis site that read OpenAI's page itself; I did not open OpenAI's page. The 20-day figure is FourWeekMBA's own count. FourWeekMBA does not allege a policy breach.
